summary: FireFusion-X harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations into an interactive burning-activity calendar. The system normalizes 2024-2025 hotspot data, aggregates observations with H3 hexagonal spatial indexing, translates VIIRS counts to a MODIS-equivalent scale, and exposes maps, calendar patterns, sensor comparisons, exports, and independent validation. A pooled ratio fitted on 2024 achieved R²=0.8168 and RMSE=5.43 on unseen 2025 aggregate cell-months. This measures cross-sensor agreement, not wildfire-detection accuracy. The dashboard also reports its main limitation: nominal 95% intervals covered only 51.3% of unseen cases. FireFusion-X is built with a FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, DuckDB analytical database, and MapLibre GL JS for geospatial visualization, enabling early warning responders, scientists, and land managers to examine historical fire patterns, unusual conditions, and critical periods within a selected area of interest.
details: FireFusion-X harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS C2 active-fire observations into a unified burning-activity calendar. The system processes 128,613,037 observations (2024-2025), aggregates them with H3 hexagonal spatial indexing, and applies a pooled ratio calibration to translate VIIRS counts to MODIS-equivalent scale. TECHNICAL STACK: FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, DuckDB analytical database, H3 spatial indexing, MapLibre GL JS, ECharts, pandas, NumPy, SciPy. VALIDATION: Temporal holdout R2=0.8168 RMSE=5.43 on unseen 2025 data. Spatial block CV R2=0.8766. Out-of-sample CI coverage 51.3% at nominal 95% (disclosed). FEATURES: Interactive H3 hexagonal map, burning-activity calendar heatmap, sensor comparison dashboard, date-range filtering, CSV/JSON export, independent validation panel. Source: https://github.com/AhmedFawzy-Ai-Dev/Harmonization-of-MODIS-and-VIIRS-Hot-Spots
